stem:
Mrs Lee's mimosa plant folds its leaves when it is touched. On a hot day, Ben's dog lies down in the shade.

Which characteristic of living things do **both** show?
options: Living things need food to survive.
working: Both react to something around them (a touch, the heat) — they respond to changes.
Watch out: Ask: what CAUSED the action? A touch or heat = a change around it = respond.

distractors.1: Neither story shows them getting bigger.
distractors.2: Neither story shows young being produced.

stem:
The table shows some information about things P, Q, R and S. A tick (✓) shows that the thing has the characteristic.

| Thing | Can grow | Can reproduce | Needs air, food
and water |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Q | ✓ | | |
| R | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| S | | | |

Which of them are living things?
working: A living thing has ALL the characteristics. Only P and R grow, reproduce and need air, food and water.
Watch out: Growing alone does not make something living.

distractors.2: Q can grow but cannot reproduce — like fire or a crystal, it is non-living.
distractors.3: Q is not living (one tick is not enough).
distractors.4: S has none of the characteristics.

stem:
Study living things W, X and Y.

Which statement about W, X and Y is correct?
options: W and X are flowering plants.
W and Y reproduce by spores.
X and Y reproduce by seeds.
working: W is a fern (non-flowering plant) and Y is a mushroom (fungus). Both reproduce by spores.
Watch out: Spores belong to ferns AND fungi — but only the fern makes its own food.

distractors.3: A mushroom is a fungus — it cannot make its own food.
distractors.4: Mushrooms reproduce by spores, not seeds.

stem:
Four statements were made about fungi and bacteria.

A Yeast is used to make bread dough rise.
B Some bacteria are used to make yoghurt.
C Mould grows faster on dry bread than on moist bread.
D All bacteria cause diseases.
working: A and B are true. Mould needs moisture, so it grows faster on MOIST bread (C false). Many bacteria are useful (D false).
Watch out: Mark T or F beside every statement first.

distractors.3: C is false — mould needs water to grow.
distractors.4: C and D are both false.

stem:

with water | Kept in a
warm place |

| B | | ✓ |

Which slice of bread will have the most mould?
options: All will have the same amount.
working: Mould grows best with water (moisture) and warmth. Only A has both.
Watch out: Mould needs water, warmth, food and air — check every condition.

distractors.1: B is warm but dry — mould needs water.
distractors.2: C is moist but cold — mould grows slowly in the cold.
distractors.3: The conditions are different, so the amounts differ.

Which of the following could be animals E, F and G?
options: E: bat · F: frog · G: dolphin
E: penguin · F: crocodile · G: cat
E: penguin · F: salamander · G: whale
E: ostrich · F: toad · G: chicken
working: Penguin = bird (feathers). Salamander = amphibian (moist skin). Whale = mammal (gives birth to young alive).
Watch out: Check every animal in the row — one wrong animal makes the whole row wrong.

distractors.1: A bat has fur, not feathers.
distractors.2: A crocodile has dry, scaly skin.

distractors.1: A centipede does not have 3 body parts, so it stops at P, not S.
distractors.2: A beetle has 3 body parts, so it cannot be P.
distractors.3: A butterfly has 3 body parts, so it cannot be P.

stem:
Study the classification chart.

Which of the following could be headings X and Y?
options: X: Cannot make their own food · Y: Can make their own food
X: Reproduce by spores · Y: Reproduce by seeds
X: Can only be seen under a microscope · Y: Can be seen without a microscope
working: Mushroom, mould and yeast are fungi — they cannot make their own food. Fern, moss and balsam are plants — they make their own food.
Watch out: A heading must be true for EVERY item under it.

distractors.2: Fern and moss reproduce by spores, so Y cannot be 'by seeds'.
distractors.3: Fern and moss are non-flowering, so Y cannot be 'flowering'.
distractors.4: Mushrooms and mould can be seen without a microscope.

Watch out: List the jobs first; flexible is not needed here.

stem:
Pam put a toy inside three boxes made of materials K, L and M, one at a time. She recorded what she saw.

| Box made of | What Pam saw |
| --- | --- |
| K | toy seen clearly |
| L | toy seen faintly |
| M | toy cannot be seen |

Which shows the materials from the one that lets the MOST light through to the LEAST?
working: Clearly = most light passes through (K); faintly = some (L); cannot see = no light (M).
Watch out: Check the direction of the order the question asks for.

distractors.1: This is least to most — reversed.
distractors.2: L lets less light through than K.
distractors.3: M lets no light through, so it must be last.

Objects of different sizes, made of the same material

Watch out: Follow the arrows: the missing box comes straight after the seed.

In which dishes will the seeds germinate?
working: Seeds need water, air and warmth to germinate. A and C have all three. Light is not needed, so the dark dish C still germinates.
Watch out: WAW: Water, Air, Warmth. NOT light.

distractors.1: C also germinates — light is not needed for germination.
distractors.2: D is too cold — seeds need warmth.

A mosquito
B cockroach
C beetle
D chicken
working: Mosquitoes and beetles have four stages: egg, larva, pupa, adult.
Watch out: B-B-M make pupae: Butterfly, Beetle, Mosquito.

distractors.1: A cockroach has egg, nymph, adult — no pupa.
distractors.3: Neither the cockroach nor the chicken has a pupa.

stem: Which diagram shows the life cycle of a cockroach?
working: A cockroach has three stages: egg → nymph → adult → egg.
Watch out: Nymph = young that looks like the adult. No pupa for nymph animals.

distractors.1: That is a four-stage cycle (beetle, butterfly, mosquito).
distractors.3: The order is wrong: the egg hatches into a nymph, not an adult.

stem:
The graph shows the number of days a mosquito spends in each stage of its life cycle.

The eggs were laid on Day 0. At which stage is the mosquito on **Day 11**?
working: Egg: days 0–2. Larva: days 2–9 (2 + 7). Pupa: days 9–12 (9 + 3). Day 11 falls in the pupa stage.
Watch out: Add the bars one by one from Day 0, including the egg.

distractors.2: The larva stage ends on day 9.
distractors.4: Adult only from day 12 — forgetting the 2 egg days gives this wrong answer.

stem: Which statement about a tadpole is correct?

distractors.2: A tadpole does not look like a frog — the frog is the odd one out among 3-stage animals.
distractors.4: Frogs lay their eggs in water.

Which parts are the poles of the magnet?

Watch out: Poles = the two ends = the two tallest bars.

distractors.2: X and Y are the middle — the weakest part.

stem:
Marcus brought each pole of a magnet near objects J, K, L and M.

| Object | Near north pole | Near south pole |
| --- | --- | --- |
| J | attracted | attracted |
| K | repelled | attracted |
| L | no movement | no movement |
| M | attracted | attracted |

Which object is **definitely** a magnet?
working: K was repelled by the north pole. Only a magnet can be repelled by a magnet.
Watch out: Repelled = magnet for sure. Attracted alone proves nothing.

distractors.1: J was attracted by both poles — a magnetic material (it might not be a magnet).
distractors.4: Like J, M could just be a magnetic material.

stem:
A U-shaped magnet is attracted to a bar magnet as shown. End A is a north pole.

What are poles P and Q?
working: A (north) attracts P, so P is south. The other end of the bar magnet, Q, is north (and it attracts B, the south end of the U-magnet).
Watch out: Touching and attracting → opposite poles. Then flip for the other end.

distractors.1: P touches a north pole and attracts it, so P must be south.
distractors.2: A magnet's two ends are always different.
distractors.4: A magnet's two ends are always different.
